slides.texte_overlay:
How to get extremely good at
conversation in your 20s
Learn to listen for the hidden topic. When someone says "I was up late," ask "Doing something fun?" Small details people drop are invitations to talk more.
Match the depth they offer. Light answer, keep it light. Personal answer, go a bit deeper. Mirroring how open someone is makes them feel safe with you.
Talk about ideas, not just events. "What do you think makes a city feel alive?" Questions about opinions lead to the best, most memorable conversations.
Feed your head every day. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and I always have something fresh to bring into any conversation I have.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. I always have something fresh to bring into any conversation.

slides.texte_overlay: Admit when you don't know something. "I've never heard of that, tell me more." Curiosity is far more engaging and likeable than pretending to know everything.
Make people laugh at situations, not at others. Light humour about shared moments brings people closer, while jokes at someone's expense push everyone away.
Remember to ask about them next time. "How did the interview go?" Picking up an old conversation shows you listened, and it makes every chat easier.
